title: Validating argument-based opinion dynamics with survey experiments

key_points.claim: Opinion dynamics uses ABMs of artificial agents on interaction networks to study consensus, polarization, and conflict.
key_points.evidence_quote: It uses agent-based computational models (ABMs) to simulate the evolution of opinions in a population of artificial agents.

key_points.claim: Classical assimilative influence models predict consensus on connected networks. Later mechanisms explain persistent plurality: bounded confidence, homophily, negative influence, opinion reinforcement, and biased assimilation.
key_points.evidence_quote: Early models (French 1956; DeGroot 1974; Friedkin & Johnsen 1990) implementing positive social influence by which opinions assimilate in interaction predict consensus whenever the interaction network is a single connected component.

key_points.claim: Empirical validation is a key open challenge. The paper links survey-experiment data to an argument-based model, calibrating the micro level and then matching macro-level opinion distributions.
key_points.evidence_quote: The empirical validation of models remains one of the most important challenges in opinion dynamics.

key_points.claim: The extended model adds an external balanced-information source. Surveyed opinion distributions are matched with high accuracy in a region of parameter space where social influence and external noise have equal impact.
key_points.evidence_quote: surveyed opinion distributions are matched with a high level of accuracy in a specific region in the parameter space, indicating an equal impact of social influence and external noise.

key_points.claim: The estimated strength of biased processing at the macro level is compatible with the micro-level estimates. The paper also presents a new method for automated classification of model outcomes.
key_points.evidence_quote: the estimated strength of biased processing given the macro data is compatible with those values that achieve high likelihood at the micro level.

reliability_notes: Full text was fetched, but I read only the abstract and the start of the introduction. Peer-reviewed venue (JASSS special issue) posted as an arXiv preprint. It covers the opinion dynamics and validation aspect of artificial societies, not artificial societies in general.
